from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        one = MathTex("1", color=WHITE)
        power_labels = VGroup(eight, four, one).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(power_labels, 'A4', 'A6', scale_factor=0.7)
        self.play(Write(power_labels))
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Improved positioning (Issue 21/33)
        formula_1101 = Text("1101", color="#00FFFF")
        self.place_in_area(formula_1101, 'A4', 'B6', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(formula_1101))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(Indicate(formula_1101), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FF00")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Synthesis and Application", [
            "Binary is an instruction set for recursive puzzles.",
            "Logical pulse controls every disk transition.",
            "This rhythm scales to any number of disks."
        ])
        
        # Load assets
        disk_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/disk.svg")
        tower_icon = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/tower.svg")
        
        # Display instruction block
        instruction_label = Text("Binary Code", font_size=32, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(instruction_label, 'A4')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]))
        self.play(Write(instruction_label))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]))
        
        # Rhythmic pulsing wave
        pulse = Annulus(inner_radius=0.2, outer_radius=0.4, color="#00FFFF", fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_at_grid(pulse, 'C4')
        self.play(Flash(pulse, color="#00FFFF", flash_radius=1.0))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]))
        
        # Disk multiplying into tower
        disks = VGroup(*[disk_icon.copy() for _ in range(3)])
        disks.arrange(UP, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(disks, 'D4', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        tower = tower_icon.copy().set_color("#00FF00")
        self.place_at_grid(tower, 'F4', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(disks))
        self.play(Transform(disks, tower))

outline.topic: Binary Logic in the Towers of Hanoi
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in computer science and mathematics

sections.title: Introduction: The Binary Basics (1 minute)
sections.content: Define the binary system using a 'Light Switch' analogy. Explain how each bit represents a power of 2 (1, 2, 4, 8...), showing that any decimal number is a unique sum of powers of 2.
sections.example: Represent the number 13 as 8 + 4 + 1, visualized as three lit bulbs (ON-OFF-ON-ON) corresponding to positions 2^3, 2^2, and 2^0.

sections.title: Mapping Towers of Hanoi to Binary (1.5 minutes)
sections.content: Introduce the puzzle: Moving n disks takes 2^n - 1 moves. Demonstrate that the disk movement sequence follows a binary counting pattern (Gray Code logic).
sections.example: For 3 disks, the total moves are 2^3 - 1 = 7. Show a table where move numbers 1 through 7 correspond to the disk that moves: 1, 2, 1, 3, 1, 2, 1.

sections.title: Visualizing the Algorithm (1.5 minutes)
sections.content: Connect the binary representation of the move count (1 to 7) to the actual physical disk movement. Specifically, the disk moved is determined by the position of the least significant bit that changes in binary.
sections.example: A robotic arm (character: 'Bit the Bot') moves Disk 1 on odd steps (1, 3, 5, 7), Disk 2 on steps 2 and 6, and Disk 3 on step 4.

sections.title: Synthesis and Application (1 minute)
sections.content: Summarize how binary isn't just for counting, but serves as an instruction set for recursive problems. Conclude by showing how this logic scales to any number of disks.
sections.example: Animation showing the disks moving synchronously with a binary counter clock, transforming the complex puzzle into a simple rhythmic pulse.
